rules.serialization: UTF-8 JSON, separators ',' and ':', no whitespace, no trailing newline, non-ASCII as raw UTF-8 (never \u escapes), the escapes of RFC 8259 with lower-case hex for other control characters, '/' not escaped, keys in the builder order below, no NaN or Infinity. Numbers are IEEE-754 doubles written exactly as ECMAScript Number::toString writes them (what JSON.stringify emits): integers below 2^53 in full, 1.0 -> 1, 0.00001, 1.5e-7, 1e+21, 2^60 -> 1152921504606847000, -0.0 -> 0. JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(body)) reproduces every body. Every string is valid Unicode and every number finite: intake refuses a notice whose webhook_context holds a lone surrogate or a non-finite number (b8/fixtures.json rules.context), so no body ever needs one.
rules.prompt.version.created: data: prompt{id,name}, version{id,version,commit_message,[commit_message_truncated],is_default,labels[{id,name,type}],created_at,created_by}, previous_version{id,version}|null, links{app,api}, then content or content_omitted (full mode only); timestamp = version.created_at
rules.prompt.label.changed: data: action, cause, prompt{id,name}, label{id,name,type}, revision, from_version{id,version}|null, to_version{id,version,commit_message,[commit_message_truncated]}|null, changed_at, changed_by, links{app,api}, then content (full mode only); action is assigned when from is null, removed when to is null, else moved; timestamp = changed_at
rules.deployment.run: B8-EVENT-CONTRACT.md section 7.1, keys in the order of section 12.5; context_dropped follows context; error keys type, code, http_status, host (present ones only); only the named notice fields are copied. run.context keys are the customer's, so they are written in the order JSON.parse gives them (ECMA-262 OrdinaryOwnPropertyKeys): keys that are array indexes (0 or a decimal integer without a leading zero, below 2^32 - 1) ascending by value first, then the other keys in received order. data.deployment.name is X-Omega-Deployment-Name decoded by the deployment_name_header rule
rules.people: {id, name} with name the display name or null; {id} when include_people_names is false; null when no person acted
rules.commit_message: scrub, then cut. Scrub: every match of the secret-shape pattern sk-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,}|whsec_[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{8,} (one alternation, leftmost first, non-overlapping) is replaced by the 10 characters [redacted], in thin and full mode, in version.commit_message and to_version.commit_message. Cut: thin keeps the first 200 Unicode code points of the scrubbed text, full the first 1,000; commit_message_truncated: true right after it when cut; no ellipsis. Cutting first could leave the head of a key (sk-p) too short to match
rules.test_events: id evt_test_<ulid>, test: true after workspace_id, nil UUID for prompt, version and label ids, names prefixed '[Test] ', dep-0000000000000000 for a deployment
rules.secret_shapes: the vectors use only 'sk-' + 8 or more of [A-Za-z0-9_-] and 'whsec_' + 8 or more base64 characters; FA's scrubber may know more shapes (owned by the scrubber, not these vectors), and masks each match with [redacted]. A shape in run context drops the whole context (context_dropped); in full-mode content it omits the content (content_omitted); in a commit message it is masked in place
rules.deployment_name_header: X-Omega-Deployment-Name (percent-encoded UTF-8, contract section 4.3): the wire value must be visible ASCII (U+0020-U+007E); each %XX with two hex digits (either case) is one byte, any other character is its own byte (a '%' without two hex digits stays as it is, '+' is not a space); the bytes must be strict UTF-8 (no invalid, truncated, overlong or surrogate sequence; a U+FEFF is kept). Otherwise intake answers 400 invalid_header, field X-Omega-Deployment-Name (contract section 5.1 step 3). Do not use a decoder that throws on a lone '%' (decodeURIComponent) or replaces bad bytes (unquote's default)
rules.full_mode: content{messages[{role,text}] or template, variables[], model}; nothing else (P3)
rules.fan_out: events in acceptance order; endpoints in id order; an endpoint takes the event when its workspace matches (or it is org-wide) and any subscription matches the type (exact or group 'x.*') and its filters; a targeted endpoint takes it without a subscription, or through its subscriptions' filters minus the deployment filter, and never twice; deployment.run.failed subscriptions default statuses to [failed, interrupted]; every non-test delivery takes the endpoint's next sequence number; an endpoint that is not enabled gets paused deliveries until paused_count reaches 10,000, then skipped (backlog_cap), both numbered; tests go only to their endpoint, with seq null
